import { Canvas, Meta } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as TokenStories from './Tokens.stories'

<Meta of={TokenStories} />

# Tokens

Every component reads its colours, radius, shadows, fonts and heights from CSS variables. The swatches below show the live values. Use the **Theme** and **Scheme** switches in the toolbar to see them change.

To change a token for your app, use `defineTheme()` or `extendTheme()`. See **Theming**. To use one in your own code, read the variable, or call `tokenVar()` in JavaScript:

```tsx
import { tokenVar } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'

<div style={{ color: tokenVar('mutedForeground') }} />   // var(--ui-muted-foreground)
```

```css
.my-panel {
  background: var(--kit-surface-raised);
  border: 1px solid var(--ui-border);
  border-radius: var(--ui-radius);
}
```

## Colours

Variables named `--ui-*` are shared with ui-sdk. Variables named `--kit-*` are the kit's own. Each colour has a light and a dark value.

<Canvas of={TokenStories.Colors} sourceState="none" />

Pair each background token with its `…Foreground` token for text on it, so the contrast holds in both schemes.

## Radius

`radius` is the default for fields and buttons. `radiusSm` is for small inner parts like list items and chips. `radiusLg` is for floating layers and containers like dropdown lists, cards and dialogs.

<Canvas of={TokenStories.Radius} sourceState="none" />

## Shadows

`shadow` is for slightly raised elements. `shadowLg` is for floating layers like dropdown lists, menus and dialogs.

<Canvas of={TokenStories.Shadows} sourceState="none" />

## Typography

`fontSans` is the interface font. `fontMono` is for codes, IDs and numbers that should line up. `fontSize` and `lineHeight` set the base text size.

<Canvas of={TokenStories.Typography} sourceState="none" />

## Control heights

Buttons, inputs and selects of the same `size` share a height, so they line up in a row. These variables aren't part of the theme API. Override them in CSS if you need to.

<Canvas of={TokenStories.ControlHeights} sourceState="none" />

components-buttons-button--docs.content:
import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { IconButton } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
import * as ButtonStories from './Button.stories'

<Meta of={ButtonStories} />

# Button

Runs an action. It comes in six variants and four sizes, takes icons on either side, and stays pending while an async `onClick` runs, so a form can't be submitted twice.

<Source
  language="tsx"
  dark
  code={`import { Button, IconButton } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`}
/>

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Variants} />

## Playground

Change the props below to see every combination.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Playground} />
<Controls of={ButtonStories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Variants

| Variant | Use it for |
| --- | --- |
| `filled` (default) | The main action on a page or in a dialog. Use one per view. |
| `light` | A secondary action that should still stand out. |
| `outline` | A secondary action next to a filled button. |
| `subtle` | Low-emphasis actions in toolbars, table rows and cards. |
| `default` | Neutral actions like Cancel or Back. |
| `danger` | Destructive actions like Delete. Pair it with a confirmation. |

The preview at the top of the page shows all six.

### Sizes

`size` sets the height from the `--kit-h-*` tokens: `xs` 28px, `sm` 32px, `md` 36px (default), `lg` 44px. Form fields use the same scale, so a button and a field of the same size line up.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Sizes} />

### With icons

`leftSection` and `rightSection` take any node, usually one of the kit's `icons`. Put a forward-pointing icon on the right and an add or action icon on the left.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.WithIcons} />

### Icon only

Use `IconButton` for a button with no visible text. It is square, defaults to the `subtle` variant, and **requires `aria-label`**, which TypeScript enforces.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.IconOnly} />

### Loading

`loading` shows a spinner in place of the left section and blocks presses. The button stays focusable, so keyboard users don't lose their place.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Loading} />

### Async click

Return a Promise from `onClick` and the button becomes pending until it settles: it gets `aria-busy`, ignores more presses and, if the action takes longer than a second, tells screen readers it's loading. You don't need a `loading` state of your own for this.

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.AsyncClick} />

```tsx
<Button onClick={() => api.savePackage(values)}>Save</Button>
```

This tracks the Promise from the button's own `onClick`. For a form's async `onSubmit`, keep a pending flag and pass it to `loading` instead.

### Disabled and full width

<Canvas of={ButtonStories.Disabled} />
<Canvas of={ButtonStories.FullWidth} />

## Props

### Button

<ArgTypes of={ButtonStories} />

Button also accepts the props of ui-sdk's Button, such as `type`, `onClick` and `focusableWhenDisabled`. `type` defaults to `'button'`, so set `type="submit"` to submit a form.

### IconButton

<ArgTypes of={IconButton} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-button` | The button, for both Button and IconButton |
| `.kit-icon-button` | Added on IconButton |
| `.kit-button--full` | Added with `fullWidth` |
| `.kit-button__section` | The left or right section, and the loading spinner |
| `.kit-button__label` | The text |
| `[data-variant]`, `[data-size]` | The current variant and size |
| `[data-loading]` | Present while `loading` is set |
| `[data-pending]` | Present while an async `onClick` runs (from ui-sdk) |
| `[data-disabled]` | Present while disabled (from ui-sdk) |

Colours come from the theme tokens: `primary` and `primaryForeground` for `filled`, `primarySoft` for `light`, `destructive` for `danger`. See **Tokens** for the full list. To restyle one button, pass `className`. The kit's rules sit in `@layer ui-kit`, so your unlayered CSS wins without `!important`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Button](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/button), which renders a native `<button>`.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space | Presses the focused button |

- Give every button a text label that says what it does: "Save package", not "OK".
- `IconButton` must have an `aria-label`. Add a `Tooltip` with the same text for sighted mouse users.
- While pending, the button sets `aria-busy="true"` and `aria-disabled="true"` and keeps focus.
- Use `focusableWhenDisabled` when a disabled button should still be reachable, for example to show a tooltip explaining why it's disabled.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep one `filled` button per view, for the main action.
- Start labels with a verb: "Add package", "Export report".
- Put Cancel (`default`) before the primary action in dialog footers.

**Don't**

- Don't use a button to go to another page. Use a link.
- Don't change the label to "Saving…" while pending. The spinner and the screen reader announcement already say it's working, and a changing label shifts the button's width.
- Don't use `danger` for actions that can be undone.

## Related

- **Dialog** and **ConfirmDialog**: footers built from buttons.
- **Tooltip**: names an `IconButton` for mouse users.
- **ActionMenu**: when a row has more actions than fit as buttons.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './Checkbox.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Checkbox

A checkbox with its label beside it, for yes/no choices and for picking several items from a list.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Checkbox } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A choice that takes effect when the form is submitted | `Checkbox` |
| A setting that takes effect immediately | `Switch` |
| One of a few options | `RadioGroup` or `SegmentedControl` |
| Several of many options | `MultiSelect`, or several checkboxes |
| A filter toggle in a toolbar | `Chip` |

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### States

`onChange` receives `true` or `false`. Use `checked` to control it, or `defaultChecked` to leave the state to the checkbox. Checkbox takes the field props (`description`, `error`, `required`, `disabled`…) like the other inputs.

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

### Select all

`indeterminate` shows a dash: some of the items it stands for are checked. Clicking it calls `onChange(true)`.

<Canvas of={Stories.SelectAll} />

### Sizes

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFCheckbox } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFCheckbox name="acceptTerms" label="I accept the terms" rules={{ required: 'Accept the terms to continue' }} />
```

The form value is a `boolean`.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

In a native form, a checked checkbox submits `value` (`'on'` by default) under `name`.

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-field.kit-field--inline` | The wrapper, with the label beside the box |
| `.kit-checkbox` | The box |
| `.kit-checkbox__indicator` | The check mark |
| `.kit-checkbox__dash` | The indeterminate dash |
| `[data-checked]`, `[data-indeterminate]` | State on the box (from ui-sdk) |

A checked box uses the `primary` and `primaryForeground` tokens.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Checkbox](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/checkbox), which follows the WAI-ARIA checkbox pattern. The label is linked to the box, so clicking the label toggles it. An indeterminate checkbox reports `aria-checked="mixed"`.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Space | Toggles the focused checkbox |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Phrase the label positively, so checked means yes: "Send me updates", not "Don't send me updates".
- Stack several checkboxes vertically, one per line.

**Don't**

- Don't use a checkbox for a setting that applies the moment it's clicked. Use `Switch`.

## Related

- **Switch**, **RadioGroup**, **Chip**: other choice controls.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './Chip.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Chip

A pill that toggles on and off, for filters and tags. A checked chip shows a check mark.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Chip } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Filters} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Filters

Chips have no group of their own: keep the checked values in state and render one chip per option. Wrap them in a `<fieldset>` with an `aria-label` (or a `<legend>`) so screen readers know they belong together.

<Canvas of={Stories.Filters} />

### States

`withoutIcon` hides the check mark.

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

### Sizes

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

## Use with react-hook-form

`RHFChip` binds one chip to a boolean field:

```tsx
import { RHFChip } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFChip name="urgent">Urgent</RHFChip>
```

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-chip` | The pill |
| `.kit-chip__icon` | The check mark |
| `[data-pressed]` | Present while checked (from ui-sdk) |

A checked chip uses the `primarySoft` tokens.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Toggle](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/toggle). Each chip is a toggle button with `aria-pressed`.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Space, Enter | Toggles the focused chip |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep chip labels to one or two words.
- Show the result of the filter straight away.

**Don't**

- Don't use chips for actions. Use `Button`.
- Don't use chips inside forms in place of checkboxes.

## Related

- **Checkbox**: for choices inside a form.
- **Badge**: a label that can't be toggled.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import { ColorPicker } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'
import * as Stories from './ColorInput.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# ColorInput and ColorPicker

`ColorInput` is a text field for a colour, with a swatch that opens a picker. `ColorPicker` is the same picker shown inline: a saturation area, a hue slider and optional swatches.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { ColorInput, ColorPicker } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Formats

The value is a CSS colour string in `format`: `hex` (default), `srgb` (`rgb()`), `hsl` or `oklch`. Typed colours in any CSS syntax are converted to it.

<Canvas of={Stories.Formats} />

### Transparency

`withAlpha` adds an alpha slider. Use a format that can hold alpha, like `srgb` or `oklch`.

<Canvas of={Stories.WithAlpha} />

### Controlled

`onChange` runs as the colour changes, including while dragging. `onChangeEnd` runs once the drag is released or the edit is committed. Save in `onChangeEnd`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

### Inline picker

<Canvas of={Stories.InlinePicker} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFColorInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFColorInput name="routeColour" label="Route colour" swatches={brandColours} />
```

## Props

### ColorInput

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

### ColorPicker

<ArgTypes of={ColorPicker} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-color` | The picker |
| `.kit-color--popover` | The picker inside ColorInput's popup |
| `.kit-color__area` | The saturation and brightness area |
| `.kit-color__slider` | The hue or alpha slider |
| `.kit-color__thumb` | A draggable handle |
| `.kit-color__swatches`, `.kit-color__swatch` | The preset colours |
| `.kit-color__preview` | The swatch in ColorInput's field |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Color Picker](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/color-picker). The area and sliders are sliders for assistive technology, and each swatch is a button named by its colour. Give a `ColorPicker` without a label an `aria-label`.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Arrow keys | On the area or a slider, move the handle |
| Enter | In the text field, commits the typed colour |
| Escape | Closes ColorInput's popup |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Offer `swatches` for your brand or status colours, so people pick consistent colours.
- Check that text on the chosen colour is still readable.

**Don't**

- Don't use colour as the only way to tell things apart. Add a label or icon.

## Related

- **Tokens**: the theme's colours.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './FileInput.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# FileInput

Picks or drops files, checks them against your limits, and lists what's chosen. It comes as a compact field with a Browse button, or a large dropzone.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { FileInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Cards} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### One file or many

Without `multiple`, the value is a `File` or `null`. With `multiple`, it's a `File[]`. A file with the same name and size as one already chosen is never added twice.

```tsx
<FileInput label="Contract" accept=".pdf" onChange={(file) => setContract(file)} />
<FileInput label="Photos" multiple onChange={(files) => setPhotos(files)} />
```

### Dropzone

`variant="dropzone"` shows a large area to drop files on. `placeholder` is its main text and `hint` the smaller text under it.

<Canvas of={Stories.Dropzone} />

### Cards

`preview="cards"` shows each file as a card with a thumbnail (or a document icon), name and size. Inside a dropzone the cards fill the area, which still takes drops. To show files that are already saved, create `File` objects and pass them as `value`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Cards} />

### Limits and rejections

`accept`, `maxSize` (bytes) and `maxFiles` limit what's accepted. import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './NumberInput.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# NumberInput

A field for numbers. It parses what's typed, keeps the value between `min` and `max`, and formats it for display (`1,250,000.00`), while your value stays a plain `number`.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { NumberInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Currency} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Money

`prefix` and `suffix` show text beside the number. `decimalScale` sets the digits after the point, and `fixedDecimalScale` always shows them. Thousands are grouped unless you set `thousandSeparator={false}`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Currency} />

### Percentages and steps

`step` is how far the arrow keys and step buttons move the value. `withControls` shows the step buttons.

<Canvas of={Stories.Percent} />

### Other units

For anything the shorthands don't cover, pass `Intl.NumberFormat` options to `format`. They override `decimalScale`, `fixedDecimalScale` and `thousandSeparator`. `locale` defaults to the page's language.

<Canvas of={Stories.Units} />

### Controlled

`onChange` receives a `number`, or `null` when the field is empty, as the user types or steps. `onValueCommit` runs once an edit is finished: on Enter, blur or a step. Use it to save, so you don't save on every key press.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

The form submits the plain number (`1250000`), not the formatted text.

### States

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFNumberInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFNumberInput name="contractValue" label="Contract value" prefix="RM" decimalScale={2} rules={{ required: true, min: 0 }} />
```

The form value is a `number` or `null`.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

Uses the **TextInput** classes, plus:

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-input__affix` | The prefix or suffix |
| `.kit-number__steppers` | The step buttons' column |
| `.kit-number__step` | One step button |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Number Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/number-input), which follows the keyboard model of the WAI-ARIA spinbutton pattern on a native text input, so normal text editing still works.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Steps by `step` |
| Shift + arrow, Page Up, Page Down | Steps by ten steps |
| Alt (Option) + arrow | Steps by a tenth of a step |
| Home, End | Goes to `min` or `max`, when set |
| Enter | Commits the typed text |

The step buttons stay out of the Tab order, because the arrow keys do the same thing.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it for values people calculate with: money, quantities, lengths, percentages.
- Set `min` and `max` when the value has real limits.
- Show the unit with `prefix`, `suffix` or `format`, not only in the label.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for numbers that are really codes: phone numbers, IC numbers, postcodes. Use `TextInput` with `inputMode="numeric"`.
- Don't add `withControls` for large values like money. Nobody steps to RM 1,250,000.

## Related

- **TextInput**: for numeric codes.
- **DataTable**: `NumberCellEditor` edits numbers inside a table.

<Meta of={Stories} />

# PasswordInput

A password field with a button that shows or hides what's typed.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { PasswordInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### New password

Set `autoComplete="new-password"` on sign-up and change-password forms, so password managers offer to generate one. The default, `current-password`, is right for sign-in forms.

<Canvas of={Stories.NewPassword} />

### States

PasswordInput takes the same field props as **TextInput**.

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFPasswordInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFPasswordInput name="password" label="Password" rules={{ required: true, minLength: 8 }} />
```

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

Uses the **TextInput** classes. The show/hide button is `.kit-input__toggle`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Password Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/password-input). The field stays a native password input. The toggle is a toggle button with `aria-pressed` and keeps the same name whether the password is shown or hidden.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Tab | Moves from the input to the toggle |
| Space, Enter | On the toggle, shows or hides the password |
| Enter | In the input, submits the form (it never presses the toggle) |

Clicking the toggle with the mouse keeps the caret in the input.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- List the password rules up front, and show which are met as the user types.
- Let the browser autofill: always set `autoComplete`.

**Don't**

- Don't block pasting. It breaks password managers.
- Don't ask for the password twice. The show/hide toggle lets people check it.

## Related

- **TextInput**: shares the field props and styling.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './SearchInput.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# SearchInput

A text field for searching. It has a search icon and a clear button, and calls `onSearch` once the user stops typing, so you don't send a request on every key press.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { SearchInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.FilterAList} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Debounced search

`onSearch` runs `debounceMs` milliseconds (300 by default) after the last change, including a clear. Use it to filter a list or fetch results. `onValueChange` still runs on every change if you need the raw text.

```tsx
const [query, setQuery] = useState('')
const { data } = useQuery({ queryKey: ['packages', query], queryFn: () => api.search(query) })

<SearchInput placeholder="Search packages" onSearch={setQuery} />
```

### With a label

Without a `label`, the input is named "Search" for screen readers. Add a label when the search sits in a form or there's more than one on the page.

<Canvas of={Stories.WithLabel} />

## Props

Takes every `TextInput` prop except `type`, plus:

<ArgTypes of={Stories} include={['onSearch', 'debounceMs', 'clearable', 'leftSection']} />

`clearable` defaults to `true` and `leftSection` to the search icon. Pass your own to replace them.

## Styling

Uses the same classes as **TextInput**. The `<input>` has `type="search"`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/input). The input has `type="search"`, so screen readers announce it as a search field, and it gets the accessible name "Search" unless you give it a `label` or `aria-label`.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Say what's being searched in the placeholder: "Search packages".
- Keep the debounce at 300ms or more for server requests.

**Don't**

- Don't add a separate Search button that does the same thing as typing.

## Related

- **TextInput**: the field it's built on.
- **Autocomplete**: when the user should pick from suggestions.
- **DataTable**: has its own quick-filter search in the toolbar.

An on/off switch for settings that take effect straight away, like turning notifications on.

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

### States

`onChange` receives `true` or `false`. Use `checked` or `defaultChecked`, as with Checkbox.

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

### Label on top

By default the label sits beside the switch. `labelPosition="top"` puts it above, like a text field's label, so a switch lines up with the other fields in a form grid.

<Canvas of={Stories.LabelOnTop} />

### Sizes

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFSwitch } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFSwitch name="active" label="Active" />
```

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-switch` | The track |
| `.kit-switch__thumb` | The moving knob |
| `[data-checked]` | Present while on (from ui-sdk) |

Built on [ui-sdk Switch](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/switch), which follows the WAI-ARIA switch pattern: the control has the `switch` role and reports `aria-checked`. The label names it, and clicking the label toggles it.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Space, Enter | Toggles the switch |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use a switch when the change applies immediately, without a Save button.
- Label the setting, not the state: "Email notifications", not "On".

**Don't**

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './TextInput.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# TextInput

A single-line text field with a label, description and error. Every kit form control shares the same field props, so what you learn here applies to the others.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { TextInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Sections} />

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One line of text | `TextInput` |
| A search box with a debounced callback | `SearchInput` |
| A password | `PasswordInput` |
| A number, money or a percentage | `NumberInput` |
| Several lines | `Textarea` |

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Field states

These props are the same on every kit input, select and picker:

- `label`, and `description` for helper text under the control.
- `error`: a message, or `true` to mark the field invalid without one.
- `required` makes the field natively required and adds an asterisk. `withAsterisk` adds only the asterisk.
- `disabled` and `readOnly`. A read-only field stays focusable and is submitted with the form. A disabled one is neither.

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

### Sizes

`size` sets the height from the `--kit-h-*` tokens, the same scale as buttons.

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

### Sections and clear button

`leftSection` and `rightSection` sit inside the field, before and after the text: an icon, a prefix like `https://` or a unit. `clearable` adds a button that empties the field and shows only while there's text.

<Canvas of={Stories.Sections} />

### Controlled

`onValueChange` receives the new text after any change: typing, clearing or a form reset. `onChange` is the native change event, as on a plain `<input>`. Use `defaultValue` instead of `value` to leave the state to the input.

<Canvas of={Stories.Controlled} />

### Input types

`type` and any other native input attribute (`autoComplete`, `inputMode`, `pattern`, `maxLength`…) pass through to the `<input>`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Types} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFTextInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFTextInput name="packageName" label="Package name" rules={{ required: true }} />
```

`RHFTextInput` takes the same props plus `name` and `rules`, and shows the field's error message for you. See **Forms with react-hook-form**.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

The ref goes to the `<input>`.

## Styling

These classes are shared by every text-like field (TextInput, SearchInput, PasswordInput, NumberInput, Select…).

| Selector | `classNames` key | Part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.kit-field` | `root` | The wrapper around label, control and messages |
| `.kit-field__label` | `label` | The label |
| `.kit-field__asterisk` | — | The required asterisk |
| `.kit-field__description` | `description` | The helper text |
| `.kit-field__error` | `error` | The error message |
| `.kit-input` | `control` | The box with the border |
| `.kit-input__control` | — | The `<input>` itself |
| `.kit-input__section` | — | The left or right section |
| `.kit-input__clear` | — | The clear button |
| `[data-size]`, `[data-kind]` | — | On `.kit-field`: the size, and which control it holds |
| `[data-invalid]`, `[data-disabled]` | — | Invalid and disabled state (from ui-sdk) |

Borders use the `input` token, the focus ring uses `ring` and `ringBorder`, and errors use `destructive`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Input](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/input) and [Field](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/field). The label names the input, the description and error describe it, and an invalid field gets `aria-invalid`. Clicking the label focuses the input. The input is a native `<input>`, so text editing, selection and autofill work as usual.

- Without a visible `label`, give the input an `aria-label`.
- The clear button is named "Clear".

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Always use a `label`. A placeholder isn't a label: it disappears as soon as someone types.
- Put format hints in `description`: "As written on the contract".
- Set `type` and `autoComplete` so phones show the right keyboard and browsers can autofill.

**Don't**

- Don't use `TextInput` for numbers people do maths with. Use `NumberInput`.
- Don't show an error before the user has had a chance to fill the field.

## Related

- **SearchInput**, **PasswordInput**, **NumberInput**, **Textarea**: specialised text fields.
- **Autocomplete**: free text with suggestions.

# Textarea

A multi-line text field for remarks, descriptions and notes. It can grow with its text and show a character count.

<Canvas of={Stories.Autosize} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

`autosize` makes the field grow and shrink with its content between `minRows` (3 by default) and `maxRows`, then scroll.

<Canvas of={Stories.Autosize} />

`showCount` shows "used / max" under the field when `maxLength` is set. The browser stops input at the limit.

<Canvas of={Stories.CharacterCount} />

Textarea takes the same field props as **TextInput**.

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

```tsx
import { RHFTextarea } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFTextarea name="remarks" label="Remarks" autosize maxLength={500} showCount />
```

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

**Do**

**Don't**

import * as Stories from './Autocomplete.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Autocomplete

A text field that suggests values as you type. Unlike **Select**, any text is a valid value: the suggestions only help fill it in.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Autocomplete } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Free text

`onChange` receives the text, whether it was typed or picked from the suggestions.

<Canvas of={Stories.FreeText} />

### No match

`nothingFoundMessage` shows while nothing matches. Leave it out to show nothing.

<Canvas of={Stories.NothingFound} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFAutocomplete } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFAutocomplete name="district" label="District" data={districts} />
```

The form value is a `string`.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

The field uses the **TextInput** classes and the suggestions use the **Select** list classes (`.kit-listbox*`).

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Autocomplete](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/autocomplete), which follows the WAI-ARIA combobox pattern with list autocomplete. Focus stays in the input while the arrow keys move the highlight.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Typing | Filters the suggestions and opens the list |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move the highlight |
| Enter | Fills in the highlighted suggestion and closes the list, without submitting |
| Escape | Closes the list and keeps the text |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it when most answers come from a known list, but others are allowed.

**Don't**

- Don't use it when the value must come from the list. Use `Select` with `searchable`.

## Related

- **Select**: when only listed values are allowed.
- **SearchInput**: a search box without suggestions.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './InfiniteSelect.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# InfiniteSelect

A Select whose options come from a paged, searchable API. Give it one `loadOptions` function and it handles the rest: it waits for typing to pause, loads the next page as the list scrolls, cancels requests that a newer search made stale, and remembers the labels of chosen values. Add `multiple` for a MultiSelect.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { InfiniteSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Loading options

`loadOptions` receives `{ search, page, signal }` and returns `{ options, hasMore }`. `page` starts at 0. Pass `signal` to `fetch`, so a stale request is cancelled. It works with any fetcher and has no data-library dependency.

```tsx
<InfiniteSelect
  label="Contractor"
  loadOptions={async ({ search, page, signal }) => {
    const res = await api.contractors({ search, page: page + 1, size: 20 }, { signal })
    return {
      options: res.data.map((c) => ({ value: c.uuid, label: c.name })),
      hasMore: res.meta.page < res.meta.last_page,
    }
  }}
/>
```

`debounceMs` (300 by default) sets how long to wait after typing before searching.

### Multiple

<Canvas of={Stories.Multiple} />

### Editing a saved value

When a form opens with a saved value, its option may be on a page that hasn't loaded yet. Pass it in `initialOptions` so the field shows its label straight away.

<Canvas of={Stories.EditSavedValue} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFInfiniteSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFInfiniteSelect name="contractorId" label="Contractor" loadOptions={loadContractors} />
```

## Props

Takes the props of **Select** (or **MultiSelect** with `multiple`), except `data` and the async props, which it manages. Plus:

<ArgTypes of={Stories} include={['loadOptions', 'initialOptions', 'debounceMs', 'multiple']} />

## Styling

Same as **Select**, or **MultiSelect** with `multiple`.

## Accessibility

Same as **Select** or **MultiSelect**. Reaching the last option with the keyboard loads the next page, and a status in the list tells screen readers while it loads.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it for lists that are too long to load at once: contractors, users, assets.
- Return 20 or so options a page.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for short, fixed lists. Use `Select`.

## Related

- **Select** with the async props: if you'd rather manage paging yourself, for example with TanStack Query's `useInfiniteQuery`.
- **MultiSelect**: several values from a list you already have.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './MultiSelect.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# MultiSelect

Picks several options. Chosen values show as removable chips in the field, and typing filters the list. It can create options from the typed text, and search and page through options on the server.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { MultiSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Limit and clear

`maxValues` caps how many can be chosen: once reached, the other options are disabled. `clearable` adds a button that removes every value.

<Canvas of={Stories.MaxValues} />

### Create options

With `creatable`, the list offers the typed text as a new option. `onCreateOption` receives the text and returns the new option, or a Promise of it, for example after saving it on the server. The option is then selected. Add it to `data` as well, so it keeps its label.

<Canvas of={Stories.Creatable} />

```tsx
<MultiSelect
  label="Tags"
  data={tags}
  creatable
  onCreateOption={async (query) => {
    const tag = await api.createTag(query)
    return { value: tag.id, label: tag.name }
  }}
/>
```

### Groups

`data` takes the same shapes as **Select**, including groups.

<Canvas of={Stories.Grouped} />

### Server-side search and paging

MultiSelect has the same async props as Select: `onSearchChange`, `loading`, `hasMore` and `onLoadMore`, plus `getOptionLabel` for chosen values that aren't in the current page. See **Select** for an example, or use `InfiniteSelect` with `multiple`. `keepSearchOnSelect` keeps the typed text after each choice, so people can pick several matches in a row.

### States

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFMultiSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFMultiSelect name="states" label="States" data={states} rules={{ validate: (v) => v.length > 0 || 'Pick at least one' }} />
```

The form value is a `string[]`.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-input.kit-multiselect` | The field box |
| `.kit-multiselect__chips` | The chips row |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Combobox](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/combobox) with multiple selection. The input is a combobox named by the label. The chips are a toolbar named by the same label, and each remove button is named after its value.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Typing | Filters the options and opens the list |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Opens the list, then moves the highlight |
| Enter | Chooses the highlighted option, or creates one |
| Escape | Closes the list |
| Backspace | In an empty input, removes the last chip |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Move between chips |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it when people need more than one value from a long list.
- Set `maxValues` when there's a real limit, and say so in `description`.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for fewer than about six options. Use checkboxes.
- Don't allow `creatable` unless new values are really welcome. It invites typos and duplicates.

## Related

- **Select**: one value.
- **InfiniteSelect**: the same with `multiple`, for large remote lists.
- **Chip**: filters as toggles.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as SelectStories from './Select.stories'

<Meta of={SelectStories} />

# Select

Picks one option from a list. Add `searchable` to filter the list, `clearable` to allow no value, and the async props to search and page through options on the server.

<Source
  language="tsx"
  dark
  code={`import { Select } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`}
/>

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Searchable} />

**Pick the right list component:**

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| One value from a fixed list | `Select` |
| Several values, or values the user can create | `MultiSelect` |
| Free text with suggestions, where any text is allowed | `Autocomplete` |
| One value from a large remote list that loads page by page | `InfiniteSelect`, or `Select` with the async props (below) |
| Two to five options, all visible at once | `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup` |

## Playground

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Playground} />
<Controls of={SelectStories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Options

`data` takes three shapes, and you can mix them:

```tsx
// Strings: each one is both the value and the label.
data={['Draft', 'Published']}

// Objects: a separate value and label, and optionally disabled.
data={[{ value: 'draft', label: 'Draft' }, { value: 'archived', label: 'Archived', disabled: true }]}

// Groups: options under a heading.
data={[{ group: 'Pavement', items: ['Flexible', 'Rigid'] }]}
```

<Canvas of={SelectStories.OptionObjects} />

### Groups

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Grouped} />

### Controlled

Pass `value` and `onChange` to own the state. `onChange` receives the value, or `null` when cleared, plus the whole option object. Use `defaultValue` instead to let the Select keep its own state.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Controlled} />

```tsx
const [status, setStatus] = useState<string | null>(null)

<Select
  label="Status"
  data={statuses}
  value={status}
  onChange={(value, option) => setStatus(value)}
/>
```

### Field states

Select takes the same field props as every kit input: `label`, `description`, `error`, `required`, `withAsterisk`, `disabled` and `readOnly`. A read-only Select stays focusable and submits its value. A disabled one does neither.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.States} />

### Sizes

<Canvas of={SelectStories.Sizes} />

### Left section

<Canvas of={SelectStories.WithLeftSection} />

### Server-side search and paging

For a list too big to load at once, search and page on the server:

- `onSearchChange` is called as the user types. Setting it turns off local filtering and shows the search field.
- `loading` shows a loader in the list.
- `hasMore` and `onLoadMore` load the next page when the list scrolls to the end.
- `getOptionLabel` gives the trigger a label for a selected value that isn't in the current page of `data`.

<Canvas of={SelectStories.ServerSide} />

```tsx
const [search, setSearch] = useState('')
const query = useInfiniteQuery({ queryKey: ['contractors', search], … })

<Select
  label="Contractor"
  data={query.data?.pages.flat().map((c) => ({ value: c.uuid, label: c.name }))}
  onSearchChange={setSearch}
  loading={query.isFetching}
  hasMore={query.hasNextPage}
  onLoadMore={query.fetchNextPage}
/>
```

If you'd rather pass a single `loadOptions` function and let the component handle paging, use `InfiniteSelect`.

## Use with react-hook-form

`RHFSelect` from `@adhamaa/ui-kit/form` takes the same props plus `name`, and wires value, change, blur and the error message to the form.

```tsx
import { FormProvider, useForm } from 'react-hook-form'
import { RHFSelect } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

const form = useForm({ defaultValues: { state: null } })

<FormProvider {...form}>
  <RHFSelect name="state" label="State" data={states} rules={{ required: true }} />
</FormProvider>
```

See **Forms with react-hook-form** for config-driven forms.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={SelectStories} />

The ref goes to the trigger button.

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-input.kit-select` | The field box around the trigger |
| `.kit-select__trigger` | The button that opens the list |
| `.kit-select__value` | The selected label, or the placeholder |
| `.kit-select__chevron` | The arrow on the right |
| `.kit-input__clear` | The clear button (`clearable`) |
| `.kit-listbox` | The popup list |
| `.kit-listbox__search` | The search field in the list |
| `.kit-listbox__item` | One option |
| `.kit-listbox__group-label` | A group heading |
| `.kit-listbox__empty` | The "Nothing found" message |
| `[data-highlighted]`, `[data-selected]` | On the item under the keyboard or pointer, and on the chosen item (from ui-sdk) |

The `classNames` prop adds classes to the field parts: `root`, `label`, `description`, `error` and `control`. Selected options use the `primarySoft` token.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Select](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/select), which follows the WAI-ARIA select-only combobox pattern. The trigger has the `combobox` role and the list is a `listbox`. The `label` names the trigger, and the description and error describe it.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown | On the trigger, opens the list |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Moves through the options, skipping disabled ones |
| Home, End | Goes to the first or last option |
| Typing | Jumps to the next option that starts with the typed text |
| Enter | Chooses the option, closes the list and returns focus to the trigger |
| Escape | Closes without choosing and returns focus to the trigger |

If a Select has no visible `label`, give it an `aria-label`.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Always give it a `label`. The placeholder disappears once there's a value.
- Add `searchable` when there are more than about 10 options.
- Use option objects with stable IDs as values, so renaming a label doesn't break saved data.

**Don't**

- Don't use Select for two or three options. Show them all with `SegmentedControl` or `RadioGroup`.
- Don't load thousands of options at once. Use the server-side props or `InfiniteSelect`.
- Don't use the placeholder as a label or for instructions. Use `description`.

## Related

- **MultiSelect**, **Autocomplete** and **InfiniteSelect**: the rest of the combobox family.
- **SegmentedControl** and **RadioGroup**: for a few options.
- **RHFSelect**: the react-hook-form version.

<Meta of={Stories} />

# DatePicker

A date field: type the date, or pick it from a calendar. The value is always an ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` string, whatever the field shows.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { DatePicker, toDateString } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Values

`onChange` receives `YYYY-MM-DD`, or `null` when cleared. `value` and `defaultValue` also accept a `Date`, or any string `Date` can read, like the HTTP date format some APIs send. They are converted to the local calendar date.

<Canvas of={Stories.ApiDates} />

To convert a value yourself, use `toDateString(value)`.

### Min and max

`minDate` and `maxDate` limit which dates can be picked. Dates outside the range are disabled in the calendar.

<Canvas of={Stories.MinAndMax} />

### Written out

`displayFormat` takes `Intl.DateTimeFormat` options and shows the date written out, like "17 November 2026". The field then can't be typed in: pressing it opens the calendar. `locale` sets the language and defaults to the page's.

<Canvas of={Stories.WrittenOut} />

### States

<Canvas of={Stories.States} />

## Use with react-hook-form

```tsx
import { RHFDatePicker } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'

<RHFDatePicker name="startDate" label="Start date" minDate="2026-01-01" rules={{ required: true }} />
```

The form value is a `YYYY-MM-DD` string or `null`.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-input.kit-date` | The field box |
| `.kit-date__input` | The typed input |
| `.kit-date__display` | The written-out date (with `displayFormat`) |
| `.kit-date__trigger` | The calendar button |
| `.kit-popover.kit-calendar` | The calendar popup |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Date Picker](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/date-picker), which follows the WAI-ARIA date picker dialog pattern: a plain text input, a button that opens a dialog, and a grid of days inside it. Focus moves into the grid when it opens and back to the button when a date is picked.

| Key | Where | Does |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Enter | Input | Commits the typed date |
| Alt + ArrowDown | Input | Opens the calendar |
| Enter, Space | Calendar button | Opens or closes the calendar |
| Arrow keys | Calendar | Move between days |
| Page Up, Page Down | Calendar | Previous or next month |
| Escape | Calendar | Closes it |

`triggerLabel` sets the calendar button's name ("Choose date" by default). Translate it for other languages.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Set `minDate` and `maxDate` when only some dates make sense.
- Use `displayFormat` when the date is usually picked, not typed, and reading it matters, like on a summary form.

**Don't**

- Don't format the value yourself before saving. Send the ISO string to the API.

## Related

- **MonthPicker**: when only the month matters.
- **TimeInput**: a time of day.

A time-of-day field, typed segment by segment: hours, minutes and, on a 12-hour clock, AM or PM. The value is always 24-hour `HH:mm`.

`onChange` receives `HH:mm` (or `HH:mm:ss` with seconds), or `null` while the time is incomplete or empty. That's true even when a 12-hour clock is shown.

```tsx
import { RHFTimeInput } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit/form'
```

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Digits | Fill the segment and move to the next |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Step the segment, wrapping around |
| Page Up, Page Down | Bigger steps |
| ArrowLeft, ArrowRight | Move between segments |
| Backspace | Empties the segment, then moves back |

**Do**

- Store and send the 24-hour value. Let the field show the user's clock.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for durations ("2 hours 30 minutes"). Use `NumberInput`.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './ActionMenu.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# ActionMenu

A button that opens a list of actions: the "⋮" menu on a table row, an Export menu, an account menu. Pass the items as data. They can be grouped under headings and carry a second line of description.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { ActionMenu } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.RowActions} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Items

Each item is `{ label, onClick }`, plus optional `icon`, `description`, `disabled`, `danger` or `href` (which renders a link). Add `{ type: 'separator' }` for a line between items.

```tsx
<ActionMenu
  aria-label="Actions for PKG-004"
  items={[
    { label: 'Edit', icon: <PencilIcon />, onClick: edit },
    { label: 'Duplicate', onClick: duplicate },
    { type: 'separator' },
    { label: 'Delete', danger: true, onClick: () => modals.confirm({ … }) },
  ]}
/>
```

### Groups

`{ type: 'group', label, items }` puts items under a heading. Leave out `label` for an untitled group.

<Canvas of={Stories.Grouped} />

### Custom trigger

The trigger is a small, square `subtle` icon button showing a vertical three-dot icon, named "More actions" by default. Pass another icon as `trigger`, with an `aria-label` that names it.

<Canvas of={Stories.CustomTrigger} />

### Header

`header` shows content above the items that isn't an action, like the signed-in user.

<Canvas of={Stories.WithHeader} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-button.kit-icon-button` | The trigger (`className` adds to it) |
| `.kit-popover.kit-menu` | The popup (`contentClassName` adds to it) |
| `.kit-menu__header` | The header |
| `.kit-menu__group`, `.kit-menu__group-label` | A group and its heading |
| `.kit-menu__item` | One action (`[data-danger]` for danger items) |
| `.kit-menu__icon` | The item's icon |
| `.kit-menu__label`, `.kit-menu__description` | The item's two lines |
| `.kit-menu__separator` | A separator |
| `[data-highlighted]` | The item under the keyboard or pointer (from ui-sdk) |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Menu](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/menu), which follows the WAI-ARIA menu button pattern. The trigger has `aria-haspopup="menu"`, and the items are `menuitem`s.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space, ArrowDown | On the trigger, opens the menu on the first item |
| ArrowUp, ArrowDown | Move between items, skipping disabled ones |
| Home, End | First or last item |
| Typing | Jumps to the next item starting with the typed text |
| Enter, Space | Runs the item and closes the menu |
| Escape | Closes the menu and returns focus to the trigger |

On a table row, name each trigger after its row ("Actions for PKG-004"), so screen-reader users can tell the menus apart.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep the row's main action as a visible button, and put the rest in the menu.
- Put destructive actions last, after a separator, with `danger`.

**Don't**

- Don't hide the only way to do something in a menu.
- Don't put more than about seven items in one menu. Group them, or rethink.

## Related

- **Popover**: for content that isn't a list of actions.
- **ConfirmDialog**: confirm a destructive action from the menu.
- **DataTable**: has row actions built in.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks' import { ConfirmDialog } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit' import * as DialogStories from './Dialog.stories' # Dialog Opens a focused task over the page, like editing a record or filling in a short form. It has a title, an optional description, a body and a footer for actions. Focus moves into the dialog when it opens, stays inside while it's open, and returns to where it was when it closes. The kit has three ways to open one: | You need | Use | | --- | --- | | A dialog with your own content and state | `Dialog` | | A yes/no question before an action | `ConfirmDialog` | | Either of those from an event handler, with no state to manage | `modals.open()` / `modals.confirm()` | ## Playground ## Examples ### Basic usage `Dialog` is controlled: you keep `opened` in state and close it in `onClose`. `onClose` runs on Escape, a press on the backdrop, or the × button. ```tsx const [opened, setOpened] = useState(false) const close = () => setOpened(false) } > ``` ### Composition A Dialog is built from these parts, top to bottom. Every part except the body is optional. | Part | Prop | Notes | | --- | --- | --- | | Header | `title`, `withCloseButton` | The title names the dialog for screen readers. The × button shows by default. | | Description | `description` | Read out when the dialog opens. Text renders in a `

`, anything richer in a `

`. | | Body | `children` | Scrolls when the content is taller than the screen. | | Footer | `footer` | Actions, right-aligned. Put Cancel first and the primary action last. | ### Sizes `size` takes a preset (`xs` 352px, `sm` 416px, `md` 512px, `lg` 720px, `xl` 960px, `full`), a number of pixels, or any CSS length. `fullScreen` fills the viewport. ### Required decisions Turn off `withCloseButton`, `closeOnEscape` and `closeOnClickOutside` when the user must pick an action in the footer. Keep this rare: a dialog people can't dismiss feels like a trap. ### Confirm an action `ConfirmDialog` asks a question and renders the Cancel and Confirm buttons for you. Return a Promise from `onConfirm` and the dialog stays open, with the confirm button pending, until it settles. It closes when the Promise resolves and stays open if it rejects, so you can show the error. Add `danger` for destructive actions. ```tsx api.deleteRoute(id)} /> ``` ### Open from anywhere `modals.open()` and `modals.confirm()` open a dialog from any event handler, with no state or JSX of your own. They need `UIKitProvider` with `withModals` (on by default). ```tsx modals.confirm({ title: 'Publish package?', description: 'It becomes visible to contractors.', confirmLabel: 'Publish', onConfirm: () => api.publish(id), }) ``` For a dialog that holds a react-hook-form form, use `FormDialog` or `openFormDialog()` from `@adhamaa/ui-kit/form`. See **Forms with react-hook-form**. ## Props ### Dialog ### ConfirmDialog Takes every Dialog prop except `footer`, plus these: ## Styling | Selector | `classNames` key | Part | | --- | --- | --- | | `.kit-dialog__backdrop` | `backdrop` | The dimmed layer behind | | `.kit-dialog` | `content` | The dialog box | | `.kit-dialog__header` | `header` | Title and × button row | | `.kit-dialog__title` | `title` | The title | | `.kit-dialog__description` | — | The description | | `.kit-dialog__body` | `body` | Your content | | `.kit-dialog__footer` | `footer` | The actions row | | `.kit-dialog [aria-label="Close"]` | `close` | The × button | | Attribute or variable | Means | | --- | --- | | `--kit-dialog-width` | The resolved width from `size` | | `[data-centered]` | Present when `centered` | | `[data-fullscreen]` | Present when `fullScreen` | | `[data-open]`, `[data-starting-style]`, `[data-ending-style]` | Open state and animation hooks (from ui-sdk) | The box uses the `surfaceRaised` token. The backdrop is a fixed 50% dark tint; override `.kit-dialog__backdrop` to change it. ## Accessibility Built on [ui-sdk Dialog](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/dialog), which follows the WAI-ARIA modal dialog pattern. The dialog sets `aria-modal`, is labelled by its title, and is described by its description. | Key | Does | | --- | --- | | Tab, Shift+Tab | Moves through the dialog's controls, staying inside | | Escape | Closes the topmost dialog and returns focus to the element that opened it (unless `closeOnEscape` is off) | - Always give a dialog a `title`. Without one, screen readers announce an unnamed dialog. - Opening by touch focuses the dialog itself, so no on-screen keyboard appears. ## Usage guidelines **Do** - Keep dialogs for short, focused tasks. Use a page for anything long or multi-step. - Make the title a clear question or task: "Delete route?", "Edit package". - Name the confirm button after the action ("Delete", "Publish"), not "OK" or "Yes". **Don't** - Don't open a dialog from another dialog. Change the content of the open one instead. - Don't use a dialog for messages that need no decision. Use a `toast`. - Don't use `ConfirmDialog` for actions that can be undone. Do the action and offer Undo in a toast. ## Related - **ConfirmDialog** and `modals`: shortcuts for common dialogs. - **FormDialog**: a dialog with a react-hook-form form. - **Popover**: for small content next to its trigger, without blocking the page. - **Toast**: for messages that need no decision.

import * as Stories from './Popover.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Popover

A button that opens a floating panel of any content beside it: a notification list, a filter form, extra details. Escape and a press outside close it, and focus returns to the button. It doesn't block the page the way a Dialog does.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Popover } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Trigger and title

Popover renders its own trigger: a small, square `subtle` icon button. Pass an icon as `trigger`, not a `<Button>`, and name it with `aria-label`. `title` is a heading in the popup and also names it for screen readers. Without a title, use `contentLabel`.

### A form inside

Control it with `opened` and `onOpenChange` to close it from inside, for example on Apply.

<Canvas of={Stories.FilterPanel} />

### Placement

`side` picks the side of the trigger to open on, and `align` how the popup lines up with it. It flips to the other side when there isn't room.

<Canvas of={Stories.Placement} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-button.kit-icon-button` | The trigger (`className` adds to it) |
| `.kit-popover.kit-popover-panel` | The popup (`contentClassName` adds to it) |
| `.kit-popover-panel__title` | The title |

The popup uses the `surfaceRaised`, `radiusLg` and `shadowLg` tokens.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Popover](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/popover). The trigger is a button with `aria-expanded` and the popup is a dialog named by `title` or `contentLabel`. Focus moves into the popup when it opens.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space | On the trigger, opens or closes the popup |
| Tab | Moves through the popup's content |
| Escape | Closes it and returns focus to the trigger |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use it for content that relates to the trigger and can be dismissed without losing work.

**Don't**

- Don't use it for a list of actions. Use `ActionMenu`, which has menu keyboard behaviour.
- Don't put a long form in it. Use a `Dialog`.
- Don't use it for a hint. Use `Tooltip`.

## Related

- **ActionMenu**: a list of actions from a button.
- **Tooltip**: a short hint on hover.
- **Dialog**: for tasks that need the user's full attention.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './Toast.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Toast

Short messages that appear in a corner and go away on their own: "Package saved", "Upload failed". Call `toast()` from anywhere, including outside components, like in a mutation's `onSuccess`.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { toast } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Kinds} />

`UIKitProvider` renders the `Toaster`, the place toasts appear, so `toast()` works with no setup.

## Examples

### Kinds

`toast(title)` shows a plain message. `toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.warning` and `toast.info` add an icon and a colour. Each takes a second `options` argument with a `description`.

```tsx
toast.success('Package saved')
toast.error('Upload failed', { description: 'The file is over 10 MB.' })
```

### Loading, then the result

`toast.loading()` shows a spinner and stays until updated. It returns an id: call another `toast` with the same `id` to replace it with the result.

<Canvas of={Stories.LoadingToResult} />

```tsx
const id = toast.loading('Exporting report…')
try {
  await api.exportReport()
  toast.success('Report ready', { id })
} catch {
  toast.error('Export failed', { id })
}
```

### Action

`action` adds a button, like Undo.

<Canvas of={Stories.WithAction} />

### Duration and dismissing

Toasts close after 4 seconds. Set `duration` in ms, or `Infinity` to keep one until it's dismissed. `toast.dismiss(id)` closes one, and `toast.dismiss()` closes them all. `onDismiss` runs when it closes.

<Canvas of={Stories.Persistent} />

## API

### toast(title, options?)

| Option | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `description` | `ReactNode` | A second line under the title |
| `duration` | `number` | In ms. `Infinity` keeps it until dismissed. Default 4000 |
| `id` | `string` | Reuse an id to update a toast instead of adding another |
| `action` | `{ label, onClick }` | A button in the toast |
| `onDismiss` | `() => void` | Runs when it closes |

Also `toast.success`, `toast.error`, `toast.warning`, `toast.info`, `toast.loading` (same arguments, each returns the id) and `toast.dismiss(id?)`.

### Toaster

Render it yourself only if you set `withToaster={false}` on `UIKitProvider`, for example to change where toasts appear.

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-toaster` | The stack of toasts |
| `.kit-toast` | One toast |
| `.kit-toast__icon` | The icon (`[data-type]` is the kind: `success`, `error`…) |
| `.kit-toast__title`, `.kit-toast__description` | The text |
| `.kit-toast__close` | The close button |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Toast](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/toast). Toasts are announced by screen readers through a live region without moving focus. The timer pauses while the pointer is over a toast or focus is inside it, so people have time to read it and reach the action.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Confirm actions people just took: saved, deleted, sent.
- Keep the title short, and put details in `description`.
- Offer Undo instead of a confirmation dialog for actions that can be undone.

**Don't**

- Don't use a toast for errors people must fix in a form. Show them next to the field.
- Don't put the only copy of important information in a toast. It disappears.

## Related

- **ConfirmDialog**: for decisions before an action.
- **UIKitProvider**: renders the Toaster.

By default (`type="description"`) the label is added to the trigger's description, so screen readers read it after the trigger's name. - It opens on keyboard focus as well as hover, after `delay` (300ms).
- Escape closes it.
- Never put interactive content in a tooltip. It can't be reached with the keyboard.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep it to a few words: name the action, or add one fact.
- Give every icon-only button a tooltip.

**Don't**

- Don't hide important information in a tooltip. People on touch screens rarely find it.
- Don't add a tooltip that repeats a visible label.

## Related

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './Loader.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Loader

Shows that something is loading: three staggered dots, or a spinning ring.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Loader } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Variants} />

| You need | Use |
| --- | --- |
| A short wait with no layout to show | `Loader` |
| The shape of content that's coming | `Skeleton` |
| To block a panel or form while it works | `LoadingOverlay` |
| A button that's working | `Button` with `loading`, or an async `onClick` |

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Sizes

`size` goes from `xs` to `xl`. `color` takes any CSS colour. It defaults to the `primary` token, and to the text colour inside a button.

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />

### In context

Pass `label={null}` when text nearby already says what's loading, so screen readers don't hear it twice.

<Canvas of={Stories.InContext} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-loader` | The loader (`[data-variant]`, `[data-size]`) |
| `.kit-loader__dot` | One dot |
| `.kit-loader__ring` | The ring |

## Accessibility

The loader has `role="status"` and is named by `label` ("Loading" by default), so screen readers announce it. With `label={null}` it's hidden from assistive technology. The animation slows down for people who ask for reduced motion.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Say what's loading when the wait may be long: "Loading work orders…".

**Don't**

- Don't show a loader for waits under about 300ms. It flickers.
- Don't use a loader where the page layout is known. A `Skeleton` keeps the page from jumping.

## Related

- **Skeleton**, **LoadingOverlay**, **Button**.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './Skeleton.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Skeleton

A grey placeholder shape that stands in for content while it loads, so the page doesn't jump when the content arrives.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Skeleton } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.ListItem} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Shapes

Set `width` and `height` (any CSS length, or pixels), `circle` for a circle of `height`, and `radius` for the corners. Build the same layout as the content that will load.

<Canvas of={Stories.ListItem} />

### Wrap the content

Wrap the real content and pass `visible`: while `true`, the skeleton shows at the content's size. Once `false`, the content shows.

<Canvas of={Stories.WrapContent} />

```tsx
<Skeleton visible={query.isLoading}>
  <ContractSummary contract={query.data} />
</Skeleton>
```

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-skeleton` | The shape (`[data-animate]` while shimmering) |
| `.kit-skeleton__ghost` | The hidden content inside, when wrapping |

The shape uses the `muted` token.

## Accessibility

Skeletons are hidden from screen readers (`aria-hidden`). Tell assistive technology that the region is loading another way, for example `aria-busy` on the container.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Match the real layout closely: same number of lines, same avatar size.

**Don't**

- Don't use skeletons for content that loads in under 300ms.

## Related

- **Loader**, **LoadingOverlay**.

import * as Stories from './Badge.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Badge

A short label for a status, a category or a count.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Badge } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Statuses} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Colours and variants

Six colours (`neutral`, `primary`, `success`, `warning`, `danger`, `info`) in four variants: `light` (tinted, default), `filled`, `outline` and `dot` (a coloured dot beside plain text).

<Canvas of={Stories.ColorsAndVariants} />

### Statuses

Map each status to a colour once and reuse the map, so a status looks the same on every page.

<Canvas of={Stories.Statuses} />

```tsx
const statusColor = { draft: 'neutral', review: 'info', approved: 'success', rejected: 'danger' } as const

<Badge color={statusColor[pkg.status]} variant="dot">{statusLabel[pkg.status]}</Badge>
```

### Sizes, icons and counts

<Canvas of={Stories.Sizes} />
<Canvas of={Stories.WithIconAndCount} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

Other `<span>` attributes pass through.

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-badge` | The badge (`[data-color]`, `[data-variant]`, `[data-size]`) |
| `.kit-badge__dot` | The dot (`variant="dot"`) |
| `.kit-badge__section` | The left section |

A badge is plain text. Don't rely on its colour alone to carry meaning: the text must say the status. For a count, add context for screen readers, like `aria-label="12 unread"`.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Keep it to one or two words.
- Use the same colour for the same meaning across the app.

**Don't**

- Don't make badges clickable. Use `Chip` or `Button`.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './Card.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Card

A surface that groups related content, with an optional header (title, description, actions) and footer.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Card } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.WithActionsAndFooter} />

## Playground

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />
<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Header and footer

`title` and `description` make the header. `actions` sit at its top right: buttons, a badge or an `ActionMenu`. `footer` runs along the bottom.

<Canvas of={Stories.WithActionsAndFooter} />

### Plain surface

Leave out the header for a plain box. `padding` goes from `none` to `lg`, and `withBorder={false}` removes the border.

<Canvas of={Stories.Plain} />

### Page sections

`component` renders a `section`, `article` or `aside` instead of a `div`. The title then labels the element, so it appears as a named region for screen readers.

<Canvas of={Stories.AsSection} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

Other HTML attributes pass through.

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-card` | The card (`[data-padding]`, `[data-border]`) |
| `.kit-card__header` | The header row |
| `.kit-card__title`, `.kit-card__description` | The header text |
| `.kit-card__actions` | The actions |
| `.kit-card__body` | The content |
| `.kit-card__footer` | The footer |

The card uses the `surfaceRaised`, `border` and `radiusLg` tokens.

## Accessibility

A `div` card is just a container. With `component="section"` (or `article`, `aside`) and a `title`, the element is labelled by the title, so screen-reader users can jump to it.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Use cards to separate independent chunks: a summary, a related list, a chart.

**Don't**

- Don't nest cards inside cards.
- Don't make a whole card clickable and also put buttons in it.

## Related

- **EmptyState**: what a card shows when it has nothing yet.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './ScrollArea.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# ScrollArea

A scrollable box with slim scrollbars that match the theme. Scrolling stays native, so touchpads, wheels and keyboards work as usual.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { ScrollArea } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Height

`height` fixes the box's height. `maxHeight` lets it grow with the content up to that height, then scroll.

<Canvas of={Stories.MaxHeight} />

### When scrollbars show

`type` sets when the scrollbars appear: on `hover` (default), `always`, while scrolling (`scroll`), or when the content overflows (`auto`). `offsetScrollbars` keeps space for the scrollbar so content doesn't sit under it.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-scroll` | The box (`[data-offset]`) |
| `.kit-scroll__viewport` | The scrolling element |
| `.kit-scroll__content` | Your content |
| `.kit-scroll__bar`, `.kit-scroll__thumb` | A scrollbar and its handle |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Scroll Area](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/scroll-area). When the area holds meaningful content, give it an `aria-label`: the scrolling element then becomes a named region that screen-reader users can find.

## Usage guidelines

**Don't**

- Don't put scroll areas inside scroll areas.
- Don't make the main page content scroll inside a box. Let the page scroll.

## Related

- **Dialog**: its body already scrolls when content is tall.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './Timeline.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Timeline

A vertical list of events: an activity log, an audit trail, or a workflow's stages. It comes plain, or as cards in SWIFTO's style, with stages alternating left and right.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Timeline, type TimelineEvent } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Activity} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Activity} />

## Examples

### Events

Each event needs an `id` and a `title`. Add any of:

- `actor`: who did it, beside the title.
- `dateTime` (machine-readable, for the `<time>` element) and `time` (what's shown).
- `description`, and `metadata` as label/value pairs.
- `status` to colour the marker: `success`, `error`, `pending`, `info`, `warning` or `neutral`.
- `icon` inside the marker.
- For workflows: `department` and `stage` (shown after the actor as "Aina, Planning & Verification"), `reason` (like a rejection reason) and `sentFrom` (`{ name, department?, stage? }`, shown as a "Sent from" block).
- `date`, shown with `time`.

```tsx
<Timeline
  aria-label="Package history"
  events={history.map((h) => ({
    id: h.id,
    title: h.action,
    actor: h.user.name,
    dateTime: h.createdAt,
    time: formatDateTime(h.createdAt),
    status: h.action === 'Rejected' ? 'error' : 'success',
  }))}
/>
```

### Stages

`variant="status"` is roomier, for a workflow's stages rather than a dense log.

<Canvas of={Stories.Stages} />

### Cards, alternating left and right

`appearance="card"` puts each event in a bordered card coloured by its status. With `variant="status"` the markers grow and show a status icon (a tick, a cross, a clock…), and the time shows as a pill. `alternating` adds SWIFTO's zigzag: a centred line, with events alternating left and right and the time on the opposite side.

<Canvas of={Stories.AlternatingCards} />

```tsx
<Timeline
  variant="status"
  appearance="card"
  alternating
  aria-label="Work order history"
  events={history.map((h) => ({
    id: h.uuid,
    title: h.action,
    actor: h.user.name,
    department: h.user.department,
    stage: h.stage,
    reason: h.remarks,
    sentFrom: h.from ? { name: h.from.name, stage: h.from.stage } : undefined,
    dateTime: h.created_at,
    time: formatDateTime(h.created_at),
    status: h.action === 'Rejected' ? 'error' : 'success',
  }))}
/>
```

The colours come from the theme. A finished stage (`success`) and the time pill use `primary`, so with `swiftoTheme` they're SWIFTO's gold, and with the neutral theme they're blue. Errors use `destructive` and pending stages use `warning`. It works in dark mode like everything else.

When the timeline is narrower than 40rem, the zigzag falls back to one column, so it still fits a side panel or a phone. You can also leave `alternating` off:

<Canvas of={Stories.StageCards} />

### Activity cards

With `variant="activity"`, cards get a dot with a soft ring, a dashed line, and a row with the `date` and `time` beside calendar and clock icons.

<Canvas of={Stories.ActivityCards} />

### Empty

<Canvas of={Stories.Empty} />

### Custom rendering

`renderIcon(event)` replaces an event's marker content, and `renderContent(event)` replaces its body (with cards, the title and card too). Your event type can carry extra fields: `Timeline` is generic over it.

`sentFromLabel` translates the "Sent from" label.

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | Part |
| --- | --- |
| `.kit-timeline` | The list (`[data-variant]`, `[data-appearance]`, `[data-alternating]`) |
| `.kit-timeline__item` | One event |
| `.kit-timeline__marker` | The dot (`[data-status]`) |
| `.kit-timeline__connector` | The line between markers |
| `.kit-timeline__title`, `.kit-timeline__actor`, `.kit-timeline__time` | The heading |
| `.kit-timeline__description` | The description |
| `.kit-timeline__meta`, `.kit-timeline__meta-row` | The metadata |
| `.kit-timeline__reason` | The reason |
| `.kit-timeline__sent-from`, `.kit-timeline__sent-from-label` | The "Sent from" block |
| `.kit-timeline__card` | A card (`[data-status]`), with `appearance="card"` |
| `.kit-timeline__people` | The actor line in a card |
| `.kit-timeline__stamp`, `.kit-timeline__pill` | The time pill, with cards and `variant="status"` |
| `.kit-timeline__when`, `.kit-timeline__when-part` | The date and time row, with cards and `variant="activity"` |

The marker size is the CSS variable `--kit-tl-size` on `.kit-timeline`.

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Timeline](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/timeline). It's a list named by `aria-label` ("Timeline" by default), and the arrow keys move between events. Times use `<time dateTime>`, so assistive technology gets an exact value. Status colours are decorative: say the status in the title too.

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Put the newest event first in an activity log, and the first stage first in a workflow.
- Name the timeline with `aria-label` when there's more than one on a page.

## Related

- **Badge**: a single status.

import { ArgTypes, Canvas, Controls, Meta, Source } from '@storybook/addon-docs/blocks'
import * as Stories from './Accordion.stories'

<Meta of={Stories} />

# Accordion

Sections that expand and collapse under their headings, like an FAQ or optional form sections.

<Source language="tsx" dark code={`import { Accordion } from '@adhamaa/ui-kit'`} />

<Canvas of={Stories.Playground} />

## Playground

<Controls of={Stories.Playground} />

## Examples

### Items

Each item is `{ value, title, content }`, plus optional `icon` and `disabled`. `defaultValue` (or `value` with `onChange`) is the list of open items.

```tsx
<Accordion items={faqs.map((f) => ({ value: f.id, title: f.question, content: f.answer }))} />
```

### Separated

`variant="separated"` puts each item in its own card.

<Canvas of={Stories.Separated} />

### Several open

Only one item is open at a time unless you set `multiple`.

<Canvas of={Stories.Multiple} />

## Props

<ArgTypes of={Stories} />

## Styling

| Selector | `classNames` key | Part |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `.kit-accordion` | `root` | The list |
| `.kit-accordion__item` | `item` | One section |
| `.kit-accordion__trigger` | `trigger` | The heading button |
| `.kit-accordion__chevron` | — | The arrow |
| `.kit-accordion__panel` | `panel` | The content |
| `[data-open]` | — | On an open item (from ui-sdk) |

## Accessibility

Built on [ui-sdk Accordion](https://ui-sdk.dev/docs/react/components/accordion), which follows the WAI-ARIA accordion pattern. Each title is a button inside a heading, with `aria-expanded`. Set `headingLevel` (3 by default) so the headings fit the page outline.

| Key | Does |
| --- | --- |
| Enter, Space | Opens or closes the focused item |
| ArrowDown, ArrowUp | Move between item headings |
| Home, End | First or last heading |

## Usage guidelines

**Do**

- Write titles that say what's inside, so people can scan them.

**Don't**

- Don't hide information everyone needs inside an accordion.

## Related

- **Tabs**: one panel at a time, with the labels in a row.
